items.item_text: 01. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree

02. Have you completed a Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) or Home Health Aide (HHA) certification program? Options: Yes, Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) | Yes, Home Health Aide (HHA) | Yes, both CNA and HHA | No, I have not completed either program.

03. How many total years of paid OR verifiable volunteer experience have you had in a health-care service environment? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year of experience | 1 year but less than 2 years of experience | 2 years but less than 3 years experience | 3 or more years of experience

04. In which of the following health care settings have you gained work or volunteer experience? (Select all that apply.) Options: School health office or educational setting | Acute-care hospital | Outpatient clinic / medical Office | Long-term-care / skilled-nursing facility | Home-health / hospice | Behavioral-health or substance-use facility | Public-health program / community clinic | Other (health-care related) | None. I do not have paid or volunteer experience providing health care services in any setting.

05. Provide your paid OR verifiable volunteer experience in a health-care service environment (if any). For each position include: • Employer/Organization • Job Title / Role • Dates (MM/YY – MM/YY) • Approx. hours per week • Brief description of health-care service duties. Type "N/A" if you have no experience in this area.
First aid, CPR, and emergency care methods and procedures
Administer basic and emergency care, and first aid in accordance with established protocols.
Provides health services and physical care procedures for students at an assigned site, including first aid, basic wound care, CPR and life-sustaining emergency care per established protocols.

Provides specialized care to individual students, including glucose monitoring, breathing treatments, and temporary, non-recurring acute personal health care for students with short-term conditions, such as toileting assistance, personal hygiene assistance (e.g., washing up or cleanup after illness), and changing soiled or wet clothing.
Receives students at the health office, documents visits and reported symptoms; provides appropriate care within protocols; refers to the nurse or emergency medical services when appropriate.
Administers prescribed medications per physician orders and District policy; verifies required consent documentation.
Observes and screens students for illness, communicable disease, head lice, and other conditions; performs routine measurements such as temperature, height, and weight.
Coordinates vision, hearing, dental, and scoliosis screenings and health events.
Instructs students on proper personal hygiene, illness prevention, and healthy habits.
Responds to inquiries and communicates updates to students, parents, District staff, and authorized individuals regarding student health, emergencies, and documentation.
Maintains health files for new and returning students, and immunization records; ensures compliance with Oral Health Assessment and TB Risk Assessment requirements.
Maintains the health office in a clean, orderly, and safe condition; monitors supply inventory and orders and replenishes first aid and clinical supplies.
Attends staff meetings and training sessions related to student health services; maintains required certifications and stays current on District procedures and applicable regulations.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Basic student health screening and measurement techniques
Universal precautions and clean and sterile treatment techniques
Medication administration and documentation procedures
Personal hygiene practices
Effective oral and written communication techniques and standards
Student information systems and standard office equipment, including email and telephone systems
Student health recordkeeping, documentation, and reporting procedures
Health and safety regulations applicable to student health services, including the California Education Code, FERPA, and other applicable laws and regulations
Respond effectively and appropriately to medical emergencies.
Screen students for health concerns and take appropriate action within established protocols.
Administer medications per physician orders and District policy.
Maintain accurate health records and prepare related reports.
Handle confidential student health information with discretion.
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with students, staff, and families.
Work independently with minimal direction.
Organize and prioritize work to meet schedules and timelines.
Model communications and interactions that respect and include all individuals and their languages, abilities, religions, and cultures.
Interpersonal skills using tact, patience, and courtesy
Operate student information systems, standard office equipment, and a computer.
Communicate policies, procedures, rules, and regulations to students, faculty, parents, and other agencies.
